open_points.subject: A01 rule 5 vs A16 rule 1 (request-check precedence)
open_points.text: A01 rule 5: "This check comes before every other check of the request."; A16 rule 1: "A request is handled in this order... size... token... known operation and fits schema... actor may call... then the operation's own checks".
open_points.question: When a request both fails the slot/flow purpose rule and also fails an earlier surface check (schema, unknown operation, authorization), which failure must be returned first?
options: Purpose check is truly global-first and can preempt schema/authorization failures.
A16 global pipeline is first; purpose is only first within operation-specific checks.
open_points.default_guess: Apply A16 pipeline first, then run purpose check first inside the operation-specific stage.

open_points.subject: A09 rule 2 path placeholder parsing
open_points.text: "every `{name}` in the path takes the input port of that name"
open_points.question: What exact grammar defines `{name}` placeholders in paths (allowed characters, escaping/literal braces, malformed brace handling, repeated placeholder names)?
options: Treat `{name}` as a simple non-nested token delimited by single `{` and `}`; reject malformed braces; allow repeated names.
Define a stricter placeholder grammar (e.g., port-name regex only) and refuse anything else, including repeated names.
open_points.default_guess: Use simple `{name}` token parsing with strict malformed-brace refusal; require `name` to match an existing input port name and allow repeats.

open_points.subject: A04 rule 6 try-selection semantics
open_points.text: "executes ... on the cases ... that the request names, all of them when it names none"
open_points.question: Does an explicit empty case list count as "names none" (run all cases) or as an invalid selection (refuse)?
options: Empty list means none named, so run all cases.
Empty list is an explicit selection of zero and is refused.
open_points.default_guess: Interpret empty list as none named and run all cases.

open_points.subject: A08 rule 5 first-failure reporting granularity
open_points.text: "A proposal is refused as a manifest mismatch, naming the first failing check in the order listed here" where the first listed check bundles multiple conditions: "record is absent, is not valid JSON, lacks `service` or `capabilities`, or its `service` field differs".
open_points.question: Must refusal detail distinguish the exact subcondition inside a bundled check, or is naming the bundled check itself sufficient?
options: Return one generic reason for the whole bundled check.
Return distinct reasons per subcondition (absent, invalid JSON, missing field, service mismatch).
open_points.default_guess: Return one bundled-check reason unless/until State 5 reason-code closure requires subcondition-level codes.
